subject: Post-discovery: multi-region performance requirements & residency follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@finosystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-discovery: multi-region performance requirements & residency follow-up

Hi Samira — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of the performance / residency points we captured and the proposed next steps so we can align with your infra/security teams. Please confirm/correct where needed.

Summary of requirements (as we understood them)
- Latency targets (p95): US: <= 200ms time-to-first-token for short responses (~64 tokens); EU: <= 250ms; APAC: <= 350ms (APAC can accept slightly higher if routed to nearest Singapore/Tokyo zone).
- Streaming: must support streaming tokens (SSE or chunked HTTP) with time-to-first-byte target above. If model returns partial tokens, app expects ~100-150ms inter-token steady-state for streaming consumer UX.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline steady-state QPS ~ 45 requests/s for the primary app, with bursts to 220 rps for 60s during batch events. Per-connection concurrency target: ~25 concurrent streams.
- Behavior on regional capacity constraints: default preference is local-region serving. Fallback to another region only with explicit legal/ops approval for PII-bound requests. Non-PII traffic may be routed to nearest region to meet latency SLOs.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU control plane/storage (at-rest), and request logs with PII must not leave EU region. Auditability and KMS integration required.

Open items we need from you
1) Confirm the p95 numbers above and whether TTFB or end-to-end generation time is the SLO you want.
2) Confirm which traffic class is PII-sensitive and must never leave EU. Is it all requests with account_id X, or only certain endpoints?
3) Would you accept a quantized/compatible fallback model if we cannot meet latency in APAC with the full model (and what floor on quality is acceptable)?
4) Share a representative payload distribution (avg tokens, 10/50/90%iles) and expected batch window for bursting.

Attachments: perf_matrix.xlsx (first pass latency/throughput matrix)

Proposed next step: 30-min technical sync with your infra + security to walk the perf matrix and residency constraints. I can do Wed afternoon PT or Thu morning PT.

Thanks — Sean
--
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0199
From: Samira Patel <samira@finosystems.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@finosystems.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: multi-region performance requirements & residency follow-up

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: the numbers look right as targets. To be explicit — we want p95 time-to-first-token as the contractual SLO (not total generation), and p99 for critical low-latency endpoints should be < 400ms in US.
- Streaming: our frontend consumes tokens as they arrive; please assume we need honest-time streaming (not delayed chunking). Inter-token steady-state should be <= 180ms for sequences > 128 tokens.
- Throughput: steady-state 45 rps is correct for the main service; bursts of ~200–250 rps are realistic during reindex jobs. We will have occasional concurrent sessions (websocket-ish) up to 40 concurrent streams.
- Residency: EU PII classification: any request containing customer_id or user_email for EU customers must be served and logged in EU-only infrastructure. We cannot accept fallback to US for that class. Non-PII anonymized requests may be routed. 

Open asks for Redwood (urgent)
A) Can you confirm mechanism to guarantee EU-only serving (private control plane + dedicated EU pool) and whether we can circuit-break to fail early when local capacity is exceeded (rather than transparently routing to US)?
B) For APAC: can you outline latency/throughput expectations from Tokyo and Singapore regions and whether you support active-active routing there?
C) Please provide SOC2 + DPA draft (we asked procurement to prep a redline).

We can do the technical sync Wed 16:00 PT — Samira and Daniel will both join.

Samira
Samira Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, FinoSystems
samira@finosystems.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Fw: Post-discovery: multi-region performance requirements & residency follow-up

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Samira's clarifying notes. Two quick asks before the Wed 16:00 PT sync: 
1) Can you validate we can provide a Dedicated EU pool with circuit-break behavior (fail early when capacity exceeded) and a documented fallback policy?
2) Karthik, what are the realistic TTFB numbers for Tokyo/Singapore for our current medium-large model on T4/A10G vs a quantized fallback (4-bit)? Put ballpark p95 numbers in the shared sheet.

I'll attach perf_matrix.xlsx with Samira's numbers annotated and prep a short agenda.

Thanks — Sean
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fw: Post-discovery: multi-region performance requirements & residency follow-up

Quick answers for Sean / Samira: 

- Dedicated EU pool: yes — we can provision a reserved Dedicated cluster in EU with its own control plane and KMS integration. That cluster can be configured to circuit-break fast (429/queue-full) when reserved capacity is exhausted; we will not silently failover PII-tagged traffic to US.
- Fallback policies: we support a per-route policy where requests are classified (PII / non-PII). Non-PII routes can failover to the nearest low-latency region or a quantized model. PII routes are locked to the dedicated region.
- SLA options: for Reserved EU Dedicated we can offer an SLO addendum: p95 TTFB <= 250ms with a 99.9% uptime SLA on the Dedicated pool. Pricing uplift applies; I'll include two commitment tiers in a proposal.
- Next step: I'll draft the capability summary and the contract addendum language for the Dedicated EU configuration and upload it to the Drive.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 08:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fw: Post-discovery: multi-region performance requirements & residency follow-up

Technical notes to bring to Wed sync (I added these to perf_matrix.xlsx):
- Tokyo (ap-northeast-1) p95 TTFB: ~320ms on A10G for the full model (avg seq 128). Singapore (ap-southeast-1) p95 TTFB: ~300ms. Quantized 4-bit fallback reduces p95 ~25–40% depending on beam/search.
- Batching: steady-state batching windows and continuous batching behavior will be critical. For 45 rps we expect effective batching (1–4 reqs/batch) which helps throughput but not TTFB. Bursts to 200+ rps will create larger batches and different latency characteristics; we should simulate with your payload distribution.
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent streaming sessions can be supported from a modest cluster size, but streaming increases memory/KV cache requirements per-connection. If many long-lived streams exist, reserve additional capacity for KV cache.
- Load test ask: please provide a 1-hour load profile with token distribution (avg/median/90th), expected percent of streaming vs single-shot, and a sample payload set. We'll run a focused load test in EU and APAC.

I'll be on Wed 16:00 PT.
Karthik
